extraction.name: BoolQ
extraction.description: BoolQ is a reading comprehension dataset of 16,000 naturally occurring yes/no questions. Each question is paired with a paragraph from a Wikipedia article that contains the answer.
extraction.creator: Christopher Clark (University of Washington); Kenton Lee (Google AI Language); Ming-Wei Chang (Google AI Language); Tom Kwiatkowski (Google AI Language); Michael Collins (Google AI Language); Kristina Toutanova (Google AI Language)
extraction.citeAs: Christopher Clark, Kenton Lee, Ming-Wei Chang, Tom Kwiatkowski, Michael Collins, Kristina Toutanova. BoolQ: Exploring the Surprising Difficulty of Natural Yes/No Questions. arXiv:1905.10044v1 (2019).
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions were gathered from anonymized, aggregated queries to the Google search engine, heuristically filtered for yes/no questions, and paired with Wikipedia pages returned in the top five search results. An additional 3,000 yes/no questions were sourced from the Natural Questions (NQ) training set.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: User-generated content data; Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Anonymized, aggregated queries to the Google search engine, Wikipedia articles, and the Natural Questions (NQ) training set.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators label question/article pairs in a three-step process. First, they decide if the question is good (comprehensible, unambiguous, and requesting factual information). Next, for good questions, annotators find a passage within the document that contains enough information to answer the question, or mark it as not answerable. Finally, annotators mark whether the question's answer is 'yes' or 'no'.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: To assess annotation quality, three authors labeled 110 randomly chosen examples; if there was a disagreement, they conferred and selected a single answer by mutual agreement. Because agreement was high, the rest of the dataset was singly-annotated.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: "Yes" answers are slightly more common (62.31% in the train set).
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Questions are gathered from anonymized, aggregated queries to the Google search engine.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Construct highly inferential reading comprehension datasets; answering user yes/no questions
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Queries were heuristically filtered to select those where the first word is in a manually constructed set of indicator words and are of sufficient length. Questions were only kept if a Wikipedia page was returned as one of the first five results. During annotation processing, only questions marked as having a yes/no answer were kept, and each question was paired with the selected passage instead of the entire document.
